name: AIFC Investment Tax Residency Programme

requirements.blocker_text: Requires at least USD 60,000 invested in AIX-listed securities or AIFC-entity share capital (USD 150,000 if invested in digital assets through an AFSA-licensed provider). The applicant must be 18+, must NOT have been a Kazakhstani citizen within the preceding 20 years, and must NOT have been a Kazakhstani tax resident within the preceding 20 years -- this route is explicitly closed to former citizens/tax residents, not open to all foreign nationals equally.
requirements.fix_path: Invest at least USD 60,000 through the AIFC (or USD 150,000 in AFSA-licensed digital assets), while meeting the non-citizen/non-tax-resident-for-20-years condition.

evidence_required.document: Proof of qualifying investment (AIX securities, AIFC entity capital, or licensed digital assets)
Proof of no Kazakhstani citizenship/tax residency in the preceding 20 years

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: at least 90 days/year to qualify for tax-residency status specifically (not a condition of the residence visa itself)

sources.title: Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC), a Kazakhstani government-established special financial jurisdiction -- Investment Tax Residency Programme: USD 60,000 minimum investment (AIX securities or AIFC entity capital), USD 150,000 for digital assets, 18+ age requirement, 20-year non-citizen/non-tax-resident condition, 5-year visa for investor plus immediate family, tax exemptions on foreign income, and a 7,000 MCI annual fee to maintain tax-resident status

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Kazakhstan). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- direct AIFC government sourcing, tier 1. GENUINE, DISTINCTIVE FINDING: USD 60,000 is a notably low investor-residency threshold compared to nearly every other investor route built in this dataset (contrast Kuwait's KWD 5,000,000, Ghana's up to USD 1,000,000, Kenya's USD 100,000) -- clearly designed as an accessible tax-residency product tied to the AIFC's own securities exchange rather than a large-capital golden-visa program. The 20-year non-citizen/non-tax-resident condition is a real, sourced eligibility gate, not a gap -- this route specifically targets foreign investors, not returning Kazakhstani nationals. family_can_work left null since the source confirms family members receive the visa/residence permit but does not state whether they gain independent work rights distinct from the investor's own.
